primary-content.note: Sourced from Tailwind's neutral-100 via var(--color-neutral-100). The one token that carries no warm hue, because it sits on green rather than on paper.

link-underline.note: Single-role. Exists only as a 2px text-decoration at 0.3em offset.

forest.note: Reverse-out sections only. Three occurrences in the codebase.

base-100.note: The neutral ramp is the project's own spine: base-content, then base-300, base-200, base-100 at the light end.

base-300.note: Every border and section rule in the system.

base-content.note: All text. Its /70, /65, /60, /40 and /15 mixes are the entire secondary-text and decoration scale — there is no separate muted token.

display.purpose: Full-viewport hero headlines only. Scales 3rem → 5.5rem across sm/md/lg. Italic on the home hero. Utility: hero-display.

headline.purpose: The h1 of an ordinary page. Utility: page-title.

section.purpose: Section h2s. Steps to 2.25rem at md. Utility: section-title.

title.purpose: Product names and category tile labels. card-title steps DOWN to 1.25rem at sm because grid cards narrow; tile-title does not.

body.purpose: Default copy. Prose pages step up to 1.125rem with leading-relaxed, capped at max-w-2xl. main p carries text-wrap: pretty.

label.purpose: Section category labels, footer column headings, the 'From' price prefix. Always at base-content/70. Utility: eyebrow.

typographyExtras.name: footer-line
typographyExtras.purpose: Address, opening hours — things the shop says, so serif.

typographyExtras.name: logo-wordmark
typographyExtras.purpose: The header lockup. The only place sans is allowed to be large.

shadows.name: flash-toast
shadows.purpose: the toast floats over whatever page it lands on, so it is the one storefront element allowed a drop shadow.

shadows.name: admin-sidebar-edge
shadows.purpose: keeps the sidebar's edge visible beside sticky form headers that scroll under it.

shadows.name: admin-page-transition
shadows.purpose: during a push/pop view transition the incoming page casts a shadow on the one beneath, as on iOS. Only visible mid-transition.

shadows.name: row-flash
shadows.purpose: part of the admin's row-flash animation, fading in to the warning badge's colours to point at the row that just changed.

shadows.name: newsletter-focus
shadows.purpose: On :focus-visible, thickens the newsletter field's bottom rule to 2px as its focus indicator. A line, not elevation.

shadows.name: overflow-cue
shadows.value: box-shadow: inset -0.75rem 0 0.75rem -0.75rem color-mix(in oklab, var(--color-base-content) 38%, transparent)
shadows.purpose: on `.admin-table-scroll` below `lg`, telling the user a compact admin table continues horizontally. A scroll-driven animation shows it only while the table actually overflows and fades it out at the last column; browsers without `animation-timeline` get no cue. Functional; keep.

shadows.name: lightbox-credit
shadows.purpose: keeps the photographer credit legible over an arbitrary photograph in PhotoSwipe. Functional; keep.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Every link, button and [role=button] state change: colour, background, border, text-decoration-color, opacity, box-shadow, transform.

motion.name: ease-reveal
motion.purpose: Hero text arrival (.hero-reveal): opacity 0→1 and translateY(12px)→0, staggered by an inline --reveal-delay.

motion.name: ease-settle
motion.purpose: Hero photography (.hero-zoom): scale(1.06)→scale(1). Transform-only, so LCP timing is unaffected.

motion.name: image-hover
motion.purpose: Product card and category tile photography on group hover.

motion.name: tile-label-lift
motion.purpose: Category tile label rises and its arrow slides in on hover.

motion.name: shy-header
motion.purpose: The fixed header translates fully out of view on scroll-down, returns on scroll-up.

motion.name: loading-dim
motion.purpose: Body-level dim to 0.7 during a LiveView click or reconnect. The 400ms delay keeps sub-400ms socket flaps invisible; un-dim is immediate.

motion.name: submit-swap
motion.purpose: Label↔spinner swap on submit buttons. Under 300ms the spinner never appears, so fast submits look instant.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: The press lands instantly; the release fades back over ease-standard. Modelled on the Nord Design System.

motion.name: no-transition-active
motion.purpose: Deliberate absence. Category-index and size-option active underlines snap with no transition — hover breathes, active is a fact.

breakpoints.name: sm
breakpoints.purpose: The typography and gutter breakpoint. Also drops the carousel focal-point effect.

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.purpose: Footer goes to four columns; admin table overflow cue disappears.

breakpoints.name: xl
breakpoints.purpose: The navigation breakpoint — desktop nav, sign-in and locale picker appear; below this they live in a drawer.

radiusTokens.name: --radius-field
radiusTokens.purpose: Inputs, selects, textareas, badges, tabs, buttons. Overridden from daisyUI's 0.25rem default — this is what makes the system square.

radiusTokens.name: --radius-box
radiusTokens.purpose: Dropdowns, modals, drawers, alerts, cards. Overridden from daisyUI's 0.5rem default.

radiusTokens.name: --radius-selector
radiusTokens.purpose: daisyUI default, kept deliberately. Shapes radios and checkboxes; a square radio reads as a checkbox, and the checkout fulfillment picker depends on the distinction.

spacingTokens.name: --header-height
spacingTokens.purpose: Height of the fixed site header.

spacingTokens.name: --header-clearance
spacingTokens.purpose: Top offset for the first block on a page, so it clears the fixed header. Used via sm:mt-(--header-clearance) / sm:pt-(--header-clearance).

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Paper Florist"**

Everything sits on warm oat paper. A single serif, Newsreader, carries the shop's voice, and its italic is the closest thing the system has to handwriting. Sections are separated by a one-pixel rule, never by a card, a shadow, or a change of background that doesn't mean something. Photographs run to the edge of the container or past it, and the interface never frames them. The page is paper; the flowers are the ink.

The palette is one warm family. Every neutral sits at hue ~75 (oat, cream, near-black), so nothing reads as cold grey. Forest green appears only where a section reverses out entirely, and the deep green primary only on things that act. One amber-honey stroke does all the interactive work: a 2px underline, and nothing else.

Density is generous and editorial. Interaction is quiet and physical: hover underlines fade in, presses land instantly with a 1px drop and an opacity dip. Motion is for arrival and photography, and almost nowhere else.

The admin is an operating tool and follows the same tokens with three deliberate differences: sans headings, bright status colours, and bordered panels.
keyCharacteristics: Warm oat paper (hue ~75) under everything; no cold grey.
Serif for the shop's voice, sans for the interface. The admin and the reference pages (FAQ, terms, privacy) are sans throughout.
Square at the token level; the only curves are radios, status badges and pills.
Hairline rules instead of cards, panels or elevation on the storefront.
One honey underline is the whole interactive vocabulary.
Photographs are full-bleed and unframed; they carry the persuasion.
Flat by default; a shadow must carry information to exist.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Every surface, text and border colour sits at hue 60–80 or ~150. Anything else is a defect, unless it is an admin status colour.

rules.name: The Admin Status Carve-out
rules.body: Admin status colours are bright Tailwind palette (emerald, amber, orange, red), re-pointed under `.admin-theme`, so a problem reads as one before any row is opened. That vividness never leaks into the storefront.

rules.name: The Honey-Only Rule
rules.body: The amber accent is a 2px text-decoration at a 0.3em offset and nothing else: never a fill, border, text colour or badge. Its scarcity is what makes an underline read as "this responds to you".

rules.name: The Opacity-Not-New-Token Rule
rules.body: Secondary text, rules and decoration are `base-content` at an opacity: roughly `/85` to `/60` for secondary text, `/50` to `/15` for faint text and decoration, `/20` and `/12` for rules. Reach for an existing step before proposing a new colour.

rules.name: The Serif-Sans Split Rule
rules.body: On the storefront, serif is what the shop says (headings, product names, prices, quotes, addresses, hours) and sans is what the interface says about itself (eyebrows, buttons, nav, form labels). A serif button or a sans product name is a defect. The admin and the reference pages are sans throughout, headings included: one is a tool, the others are documents people consult rather than pages that persuade.

rules.name: The Open Price Rule
rules.body: A price is never smaller or fainter than what it prices: serif, upright, full `base-content`, `text-lg` or larger beside a title. Storefront prices go through `Format.storefront_price/2`, which drops the cents on whole euros.

rules.name: The Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: A category label above a heading is the eyebrow at `/70`. Never a smaller heading, a coloured chip or a pill.

rules.name: The Balanced Heading Rule
rules.body: Every heading utility carries `text-balance`, and body copy `text-wrap: pretty`. Swedish and Finnish strings run much longer than English and break first.

rules.name: The Rule-Not-Card Rule
rules.body: Sections separate with a one-pixel rule. Between full-width page sections it is ink; inside content it is `base-content/12`. Never a card, a margin-only gap or an alternating background. A background change (`cream`, `forest`) is reserved for a section that is genuinely a different kind of thing.

rules.name: The Full-Bleed Rule
rules.body: Photographs run to the container edge or past it, and are never framed with a border, radius, shadow or caption box. The one exception is the contact page's portrait of Jennie, a circle beside her details on phones, like an avatar.

rules.name: The Functional-Shadow Rule
rules.body: A shadow must answer "what would the user not know without this?" Floating layers, overflow and legibility over photography qualify. Cards, buttons, inputs, tiles and images do not.

rules.name: The Gradient-For-Legibility Rule
rules.body: Text set over a photograph on a page is made legible by a bottom-up gradient scrim (`from-black/50 via-black/15 to-transparent`), never a solid box, a blur panel or a text shadow. The lightbox credit is the exception: there is no room for a scrim.

rules.name: The Square Edge Rule
rules.body: Radius is `0`, set at the token (`--radius-field` and `--radius-box`), so markup never has to say so. Two exceptions: `--radius-selector` keeps daisyUI's `0.5rem`, because a square radio reads as a checkbox and status badges read as tags; and `rounded-full`, for things whose roundness is their meaning (count badges, avatars, dots, the contact portrait). `rounded-full` is the only radius utility allowed; `DesignRulesTest` enforces it.

rules.name: The Orphan Rule
rules.body: A hand-written value that duplicates a token is a future defect. A `0.25rem` once hand-matched to daisyUI's old field radius went unnoticed until the token moved, and a soft radio card then sat above a square input in the same form. If a token already sets the value, don't type it.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Borders are 1px. A boundary that needs more weight needs a different surface, not a thicker border. Weight comes from colour: ink for the rule between full-width page sections, `base-content/12` for every rule inside content and in the admin, and `base-content/20` for the admin navigation's edge. Never draw a line in `base-300`; `DesignRulesTest` enforces it.

rules.name: The Press Rule
rules.body: Every pressable control lands instantly (`opacity: 0.9`, `translate: 0 1px`, no transition) and fades back over 150ms on release. No scale, ripple or colour flash.

rules.name: The Breathe-Don't-Pop Rule
rules.body: Hover underlines are always present and transparent; only their colour transitions in. Active underlines snap. Hover is an invitation; active is a fact.

rules.name: The Quiet Disconnect Rule
rules.body: While LiveView is disconnected, the page dims to 0.7 after 400ms, so brief socket flaps never show, and stops taking clicks at once. The "Connection lost" toast stays crisp. Nothing else dims the page.

dos: Do set every new storefront heading in Newsreader, and every label, button and nav item in Open Sans.
Do separate sections with a rule, and reach for `cream` or `forest` only when a section is genuinely different.
Do let the radius tokens carry squareness.
Do express secondary text and decoration as an existing opacity step on `base-content`.
Do run photographs full-bleed and unframed, with the gradient scrim for any text over them.
Do guard every animation with `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`.
Do give a visually replaced control its focus ring back through `:has(input:focus-visible)`.
Do recolour the focus ring with `--focus-color` when green would vanish against the surface.
donts: Don't let the honey accent become anything but the underline.
Don't add a shadow that doesn't answer "what would the user not know without this?".
Don't wrap storefront content in a card, a panel or a bordered box.
Don't introduce a colour outside hue 60–80 or ~150, except admin status colours.
Don't drift toward the generic florist template: no pastel pinks, script fonts, pill buttons, heart icons, soft drop shadows or stock bouquet photography.
Don't bring SaaS dashboard chrome onto the storefront: no cards-in-cards, elevated panels, gradient CTAs or coloured status pills.
Don't reach for luxury pastiche: no thin all-caps sans at large sizes, no black-and-gold, no borrowed-prestige letter-spacing.
Don't use any radius utility but `rounded-full`, or draw a line in `base-300`.
Don't hand-write a value a token already sets.
